extracted.intended_audience: doctoral students applying for NIA/NIH F99/K00 Transition to Aging Research fellowships, their mentors, and institutional grant administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation criteria and reviewer guidance used by an NIA Special Emphasis Panel to assess F99/K00 Transition to Aging Research for Predoctoral Students applications, including applicant, mentors, training plan, institutional environment, human subjects protections, inclusion, and budget considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the applicant's qualifications, productivity, prior training, academic performance, letters of support, and commitment to the proposed research and career goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers note strengths such as strong academic performance, evidence of scientific productivity (publications, abstracts), enthusiastic letters of support, completion of program milestones, and clear, well-reasoned training goals. Weaknesses include lack of experience in specific methods (e.g., primary data collection, structured interviews) or insufficient demonstration of certain domain knowledge. Examples from critiques: 'The applicant is pursuing a PhD... exhibits strong academic performance... provides evidence of scientific productivity'; 'applicant’s relative lack of experience in primary data collection' and 'the prior concern regarding a lack of publication record has been addressed.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsors, Collaborators, and Consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the mentoring team: appropriateness, interdisciplinarity, expertise relevant to training aims, mentoring track record, and coordination among mentors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strength indicators include an interdisciplinary team with established mentoring track records, clear plans for transition to K00 mentors, and additions made in response to prior reviews. Weaknesses can include missing expertise needed for proposed activities (e.g., mHealth/platform development), lack of clarity about roles or how the full team will coordinate, and concerns about very large teams needing synthesis of individual responsibilities. Examples: 'The sponsors and collaborators are a strong interdisciplinary team...'; 'the mentoring team is very large; synthesis of respective training from the many members is still unclear.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Training Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the planned research and training activities for F99 and K00 phases: clarity of aims, appropriateness of methods, feasibility, timeline, and connection between training activities and research aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers look for well-developed training plans, clear aims, appropriate methods (e.g., multi-level modeling, structural equation modeling, secondary data analysis), and inclusion of didactic and experiential training (clinical internships, neuroimaging methods, clinical trial methods). Weaknesses include overly many/unjustified hypotheses, insufficient detail on interpretation of results, lack of contingency plans/troubleshooting for potential pitfalls, unclear sample size justification (e.g., 'It is not clear how this sample size was arrived at and if n=8 in each group would be sufficient'), and lack of detail on planned interventions/technologies for K00. Positive examples: 'Training Activities and Timeline table is excellent; it details the training goals, the sponsor/mentor, and the years performed.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the applicant's potential to benefit from the proposed training and to become an independent investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicators include demonstrated motivation, increased productivity (publications since prior submission), evidence of gaining relevant skills, and strong reference letters. Reviewers cite improvements in the applicant's record and alignment of training activities with career goals as evidence of high training potential. Example comments: 'The applicant demonstrates significant training potential and the training plan is very strong.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Environment & Commitment to Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of institutional resources, institutional support letters, availability of cores/centers, and the suitability of the institution(s) to provide the proposed training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths include access to relevant centers/cores (e.g., AD Research Center), strong doctoral programs, detailed institutional support letters, and demonstrated commitment across both F99 and K00 institutions. Weaknesses are generally absence of such supports or unclear institutional commitment. Example: 'The environments for both the F99 and K00 phases are strong.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of human subjects protections: identification of risks and adequacy of protections and procedures described in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review outcome language used on the page: 'Acceptable Risks and Adequate Protections.' Reviewers check that protections are described and adequate for the planned studies. Top-matter flags (e.g., '30-Human subjects involved - Certified, no SRG concerns') indicate reviewer considerations. Concerns would be noted if protections were inadequate or risks unmitigated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion Plans (Sex/Gender, Race/Ethnicity, Age)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plans for inclusion of women, minorities, and inclusion across the lifespan, with justification of distributions where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers expect scientific justification of distributions for sex/gender, race/ethnicity, and age-based inclusion/exclusion. The document records determinations such as 'Distribution justified scientifically' for Sex/Gender and Race/Ethnicity and gives sample statistics (e.g., 'Of the 8,334 human subjects, 52% are women; at least 21% are underrepresented minorities; no participants under age 18'). Inclusion plans are judged Acceptable when justification is adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the application addresses all required components of RCR training for the trainee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard expectation is that required components are addressed; reviewers mark as 'Acceptable' when satisfied. Example: 'Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research: Acceptable. The applicant has addressed all required components.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of plans for sharing resources, data, and materials produced under the award, when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers note applicability; for this application the plan is noted as 'Not Applicable.' When applicable, reviewers assess adequacy and compliance with NIH expectations for data/material sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the requested budget and period of support are reasonable and appropriate to accomplish the proposed training and research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may recommend the budget 'as requested' or suggest adjustments. Example: 'Budget and Period of Support: Recommend as Requested.' Budgetary concerns would be called out if requests were unreasonable or unsupported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact / Scoring Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of overall impact (priority) score that reflects reviewers' assessment of the likelihood that the proposed training will exert a sustained, powerful influence on the applicant's future research career.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring is numeric: individual reviewers give overall scores on a 1-9 scale which are averaged and multiplied by 10 to produce the impact score (e.g., Impact Score = average overall score * 10). Criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting and are not discussed specifically at the review meeting or calculated into the overall impact score. Some applications also receive a percentile ranking. Example note: 'The impact/priority score is calculated after discussion ... averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers ... and multiplying by 10.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Health Relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the project's relevance to public health, i.e., the potential of the proposed research/training to contribute to prevention, treatment, or understanding of important health issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must include a Public Health Relevance statement; reviewers evaluate whether the proposed work meaningfully contributes to public health goals. Example from application: 'The proposed dissertation work will contribute to fundamental knowledge ... contextualized the role of technology use ... inform the development of a technology-facilitated community-based intervention program to reduce social isolation and prevent cognitive decline among older adults.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission Responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of how well a resubmitted application addresses critiques from prior review(s) and whether the introduction and revisions comprehensively respond to previous comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For resubmissions, reviewers look for thorough, thoughtful responses to earlier critiques and evidence of strengthened application components (e.g., added mentors, more detailed training plans). Example comments: 'This resubmission application... provided thorough and satisfactory responses to previous critiques.' and 'The introduction to the resubmission is thorough and details... comprehensive inclusions based on initial commentary.'
